description: regex + lexicons + spaCy en_core_web_sm NER — the strongest reasonable non-model baseline

comparison.verdict: Adding NER closes 0.071 of a 0.489 gap. The adapter still wins by 0.418 strict F1.

notes: The four name-like labels move off zero to roughly 0.38-0.43 F1 — real, but far below the adapter.

Relaxed F1 rises more than strict (0.4632 -> 0.5939 vs 0.4299 -> 0.5006), which locates the weakness precisely: spaCy finds the right REGIONS but the boundaries and the GIVENNAME/SURNAME split are wrong. Gold occasionally treats two words as one GIVENNAME ('Vera-Maria Kélia'), which a token-position heuristic cannot know.

Precision FELL from 0.715 to 0.599 when spaCy was added. It buys recall (0.307 -> 0.430) at a cost in precision — the usual NER trade, and worth recording rather than presenting only the F1 improvement.
CARDINAL is deliberately unmapped: it would have to guess between AGE and BUILDINGNUM, and guessing costs precision on both.
This is now a serious baseline rather than a regex demo, so the 0.418 gap is a much firmer claim than the earlier 0.489 upper bound.
